answer: Agents can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a bond in a shared ledger and earn trust through repeated, cross-checked trades. Honest peers challenge claims, while proven fraud triggers automatic slashing and ejects the identity; splitting capital across many fake agents therefore multiplies the collateral an attacker must lock and risks losing it. An ember of reputation may grow on one island, but it cannot be cheaply copied into every pearl market.
